harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 (Alpine Linux 3.23) for SSH key-only access: created a locked-password opsadmin account, installed the given ed25519 public key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, and hardened sshd_config (PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, PermitEmptyPasswords no, PubkeyAuthentication yes). Validated with sshd -t / sshd -T and restarted sshd. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id 3aea70b1-c2e6-484b-a552-7bfdbef2a6c4, sshd started, key present), issued a native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed a new boot_id (95d963d1-6df8-4da3-a53d-42cdf80fc196) proving an actual restart, and verified opsadmin account, authorized_keys, and key-only sshd config all survived with sshd running and listening post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Alpine 3.23.3) and existing sshd_config/user state
Created opsadmin user with adduser -D (password locked by default)
Installed provided ed25519 public key into /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct ownership/permissions
Edited /etc/ssh/sshd_config to require pubkey auth only (disabled password, keyboard-interactive, empty passwords); removed unsupported UsePAM directive for this musl/no-PAM sshd build
Validated config with sshd -t, restarted sshd via rc-service, confirmed effective settings with sshd -T
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, sshd status, authorized_keys presence)
Issued native reboot on node1, polled until command execution was available again
Verified changed boot_id proving actual restart, and re-verified sshd health, opsadmin account, authorized_keys, and key-only auth config post-restart

evidence.requirement: opsadmin configured with SSH public key access
evidence.summary: Created opsadmin user and installed the exact provided ed25519 key into /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct permissions/ownership.

evidence.requirement: SSH restricted to key-based authentication only
evidence.summary: sshd_config edited and validated (sshd -t), sshd restarted, and sshd -T confirms effective PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, PermitEmptyPasswords no, PubkeyAuthentication yes; port 22 confirmed listening and enabled at boot via rc-update.
Captured boot_id 3aea70b1-c2e6-484b-a552-7bfdbef2a6c4, uptime, sshd started status, and authorized_keys presence prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Native reboot issued (stream closed as node went down), then polling recovered with new boot_id 95d963d1-6df8-4da3-a53d-42cdf80fc196, proving an actual OS restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and configuration
evidence.summary: After restart: sshd service started and listening on :22, opsadmin account and locked password intact, authorized_keys content unchanged, and sshd -T confirms key-only auth settings persisted.
